facts.statement: Fossils of Kayentavenator were recovered from the Kayenta Formation in northeastern Arizona and described in 2010.
facts.quote: Fossils were recovered from the Kayenta Formation of northeastern Arizona, and were described in 2010.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Kayentavenator elysiae is a juvenile that would have stood about 0.5 meters high at the hip.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of K. elysiae is a juvenile, as shown by unfused neural spines and would have stood about 0.5 m high at the hip.

facts.statement: Kayentavenator is distinguished from the contemporary Dilophosaurus by the presence of a pubic fenestra.
facts.quote: The inclusion of a pubic fenestra is one of the characteristics that Gay uses to set Kayentavenator apart from the contemporaneous, and better known Dilophosaurus.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Kayentavenator outside of Coelophysidae and closer to Allosaurus.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis of the remains showed Kayentavenator to lie outside of Coelophysidae, and was closer to Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Kayentavenator is considered the oldest known tetanuran from North America.
facts.quote: This would make Kayentavenator the oldest known tetanuran from North America.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Kayentavenator is a validly named taxon and whether it is a tetanurine.
facts.quote: Mortimer (2010) noted the uncertainty of whether Kayentavenator is a validly named taxon based on the rules of ICZN and the absence of published evidence that Kayentavenator is the same taxon as S. kayentakatae, while questioning whether Kayentavenator is a tetanurine.

facts.statement: Some researchers have treated Kayentavenator as a junior synonym of Megapnosaurus kayentakatae.
facts.quote: In the 2012 conference abstract, Martin Ezcurra treated Kayentavenator as a junior synonym of S. kayentakatae based on his unpublished phylogenetic matrix. In 2017, Ezcurra treated the holotype of Kayentavenator as a specimen of S. kayentakatae.

facts.statement: The Kayentavenator fossils are estimated to date from approximately 199 to 182 million years ago.
facts.quote: It has been surmised that the Kayenta Formation was deposited during the Sinemurian and Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic Period or approximately 199 to 182 million years ago.

facts.statement: During the Early Jurassic, the environment of Kayentavenator experienced rainy summers and dry winters.
facts.quote: During the Early Jurassic period, the land that is now the Kayenta Formation experienced rainy summers and dry winters.

facts.statement: Animals in Kayentavenator's habitat were adapted to a seasonal climate with abundant water in streams, ponds, and lakes.
facts.quote: The animals were adapted to a seasonal climate and abundant water could be found in streams, ponds and lakes.

facts.statement: Kayentavenator is classified as a saurischian theropod within the family Tetanurae.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Saurischia subordo: Theropoda unranked_familia: Tetanurae

facts.statement: Kayentavenator lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 203 to 197 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 203 a 197 millones de años, entre el Hettangiense y el Sinemuriense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Kayentavenator elysiae is a juvenile that measured approximately 1.1 meters in height at the hip.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de K. elysiae es un juvenil, como lo demuestran las espinas neurales sin fusionar, y se ha calculado que medía 1,1 metros de altura en la cadera.

facts.statement: The adult size of Kayentavenator is unknown, but it is estimated to have reached a maximum of 3 to 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: El tamaño adulto de Kayentavenator es desconocido, pero se cree que pudo medir un máximo de 3-3,5 m.

facts.statement: The only known fossils of Kayentavenator were excavated by the University of California Museum of Paleontology in the Navajo Nation, Arizona.
facts.quote: Los únicos fósiles conocidos de Kayentavenator fueron excavados por el Museo de Paleontología de la Universidad de California de la Nación Navajo en Arizona.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis shows Kayentavenator lies outside Coelophysidae and is closer to Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico de los restos mostró a Kayentavenator por fuera de Coelophysidae, y estando más cerca de Allosaurus.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Kayentavenator, UCMP V128659, was recovered from the Facies Silty member of the Kayenta Formation in northeastern Arizona.
facts.quote: El único espécimen conocido de Kayentavenator , UCMP V128659, fue recuperado del miembro de Facies Silty de la formación Kayenta, en el noreste de Arizona.

facts.statement: Researchers assume the Kayenta Formation was deposited during the Sinemurian and Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic, approximately 199 to 182 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se ha supuesto que la formación Kayenta fue depositada durante las etapas Sinemuriense y Pliensbachiense del Período Jurásico temprano o hace aproximadamente 199 a 182 millones de años.

facts.statement: During the Early Jurassic, the land now forming the Kayenta Formation experienced rainy summers and dry winters.
facts.quote: Durante el período Jurásico temprano, la tierra que ahora es la formación Kayenta experimentó veranos lluviosos e inviernos secos.

facts.statement: Kayentavenator shared its paleoenvironment with other dinosaurs, including various theropods like Dilophosaurus and Coelophysis kayentakatae, the basal sauropodomorph Sarahsaurus, heterodontosaurids, and armored dinosaurs Scelidosaurus and Scutellosaurus.
facts.quote: Kayentavenator compartió su paleoambiente con otros dinosaurios, como varios terópodos, como Dilophosaurus , Coelophysis kayentakatae y el terópodo "Shake N Bake", el sauropodomorfo basal Sarahsaurus , heterodontosauridos y los dinosaurios blindados Scelidosaurus y Scutellosaurus.

facts.statement: Vertebrates present in the Kayenta Formation during the time of Kayentavenator included Hybodontidae sharks, indeterminate bony fish, lungfish, salamanders, the frog Prosalirus, the caecilian Eocaecilia, the turtle Kayentachelys, a sphenodontid reptile, various lizards, and the pterosaur Rhamphinion.
facts.quote: Vertebrados presentes en la Formación Kayenta en el momento de Kayentavenator incluyen tiburones Hybodontidae, peces óseos indeterminado, pulmonados, salamandras, la rana Prosalirus, el Caeciliidae Eocaecilia , la tortuga Kayentachelys , un reptil esfenodontido, diferentes lagartos y pterosaurios Rhamphinion.

facts.statement: Vertebrate trace fossils from this area included coprolites and tracks of therapsids, lizard-like animals, and dinosaurs, providing evidence that these animals were also present.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de trazas de vertebrados de esta área incluyeron coprolitos y las huellas de terápsidos , animales similares a lagartos y dinosaurios, que proporcionaron evidencia de que estos animales también estaban presentes.

facts.statement: Kayentavenator belongs to the parent group Tetanurae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tetanurae

facts.statement: Kayentavenator is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Kayentavenator is Kayentavenator elysiae.
facts.quote: Type species: Kayentavenator elysiae

facts.statement: The time range for Kayentavenator is from the Sinemurian to the Pliensbachian, between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Pliensbachian (199.5 to 184.2 million years ago)
